shorts.title: KPI Green's ₹2,410 Cr wind deal: who pays?
These wind farms out-earn KPI Green

beats.say: KPI Green Energy has agreed to buy five hundred and seven point nine megawatts of working wind farms, for two thousand four hundred and ten crore rupees in cash. It's the company's biggest deal yet, and its first in wind. But the filing leaves out one thing: who pays, and how. By the end of this video you'll know what KPI Green is buying, what it costs, and the three numbers the filings don't give.

beats.say: On the twenty ninth of September, KPI Green signed a binding offer for one hundred percent of two companies: Alfanar Energy, with three hundred and one point four megawatts, and Netra Wind, with two hundred and six point five. Both run wind farms at Bhuj, in Gujarat's Kutch corridor.
beats.cap: On 29 September, KPI Green signed a binding offer for 100% of two companies: Alfanar Energy, with 301.4 MW, and Netra Wind, with 206.5 MW. Both run wind farms at Bhuj, in Gujarat's Kutch corridor.
cues: On 29 September, KPI Green signed a binding offer for 100% of two companies:
Alfanar Energy, with 301.4 MW, and Netra Wind, with 206.5 MW.
Both run wind farms at Bhuj, in Gujarat's Kutch corridor.

beats.say: Alfanar has been running since March twenty twenty one, Netra since March twenty twenty four. Both sell their power to SECI, the government's Solar Energy Corporation, under twenty five year contracts. On a capacity weighted basis, about twenty one years are left.
beats.cap: Alfanar has been running since March 2021, Netra since March 2024. Both sell their power to SECI, the government's Solar Energy Corporation, under 25-year contracts. On a capacity-weighted basis, about 21 years are left.

beats.say: The price is an enterprise value of two thousand four hundred and ten crore rupees, paid in cash. The deal should close by the twenty eighth of February twenty twenty seven, once lenders and regulators approve.
beats.cap: The price is an enterprise value of ₹2,410 crore, paid in cash. The deal should close by 28 February 2027, once lenders and regulators approve.

beats.say: Start with the price per megawatt. Two thousand four hundred and ten crore, divided by five hundred and seven point nine megawatts, is about four point seven five crore rupees per megawatt. That's our arithmetic, for capacity that's already running.

beats.say: Now the revenue. In the last full year reported, Alfanar's turnover was one hundred and sixty eight point five crore rupees and Netra's one hundred and nine crore. Together, about two hundred and seventy seven crore.

beats.say: Here's the surprising part. KPI Green's own revenue from selling power and services was two hundred and forty eight crore rupees in the whole of last year. The two wind farms it's buying earn more than that.

beats.say: That's because most of KPI Green's revenue still comes from building solar plants for others. In the June quarter, that was five hundred and seventy seven crore of six hundred and ninety four crore. This deal tilts the mix towards long term contracted power.
